why: Splitting an ordered array into exactly k contiguous groups to minimise a sum of per-group costs is partition DP: dp[w][i] = best cost for the first i campaigns in w weeks, where the last week is some suffix j..i-1 costing its maximum.
hints: Campaigns stay in order and each week is a contiguous block. If you fix where the last week starts, what subproblem is left?
dp[w][i] = min over j < i of dp[w-1][j] + max(costs[j..i-1]). Grow the last block leftward from i-1 so its maximum updates in O(1).
Fill w = 1..k, i = w..n, j from i-1 down to w-1 with a running maximum. O(k * n^2) time, O(n) space per layer (a monotonic stack brings it to O(k * n) if n is large).
pitfalls: Every week must have at least one campaign, so j ranges from w-1 upward and dp[w][i] is invalid when i < w.
Greedily isolating the biggest costs does not work; the maximum of a block depends on what else is in it.
With k = 1 the answer is just the overall maximum; with k = n it is the sum.
constraints:
• 1 <= numberOfWeeks <= campaignCosts.length
  • Numeric bounds are not stated in the source. Reasonable: 1 <= campaignCosts.length <= 500, 1 <= campaignCosts[i] <= 10^5
  • Campaign order must be preserved.
